title: Riches
tagline: An endgame money guide: arrive at Charting the Unknown rich, then make the DLC's ships, leases and islands pay.
asOf: Current to Charting the Unknown · patch 2.04.02 · November 2026

metrics.label: Return
metrics.blurb: What it pays next to the other methods, on the best documented figure. Converted to Camp Funds where the guide shows the sum; not rated where nothing is documented.

metrics.label: Effort
metrics.blurb: Hands-on time per payout. Tier I runs while you are away; Tier V needs you at the controller for every coin.

metrics.label: Setup
metrics.blurb: What it takes to start: funds, quests, staff. Tier I is available now and cheap; Tier V is a long chain or a fortune.

metrics.label: Scale
metrics.blurb: How far it grows when you reinvest or stack multipliers. Tier I compounds; Tier V stays the size it starts.

rules.text: Management methods run through camp, staff and assets; Player Control methods are things Kliff does by hand. Each is ranked against its own class.

rules.lead: Effort and Setup read like the rest.
rules.text: Tier I is always the good end: Tier I Effort runs while you are away, Tier I Setup can start today.
marks a metric nothing documents, such as Return on a castle or an island. It is never a default Tier III.
Patch notes, guide text, a guide's in-game screenshot, or a player report. A player report is one player's result and is labelled so.
Ratings stand as of 2.04.02. Nerfs, fixes and unconfirmed figures are listed under Watch out on each plate.

route.title: The Route
route.blurb: Eight phases, in order. Each one raises what the next earns: multipliers before income, income before conversion, conversion before the DLC's big purchases.
route.premise: You have finished the main story through Journey's End and own Charting the Unknown without starting it. Your camp is at Howling Hill with a working roster.

phases.label: Arm the multipliers
phases.why: Golden Beer doubles every dispatch payout and Blessings add up to +200% in a region. Both apply to every cycle you run after them, so they come before any income.

steps.text: Clear the Demeniss houses to House Byron and take the beer from Mazzul at Burnhand Quarry. Holding it is enough.
Donate to the church of the region your best dispatches run in; about 110,000 buys +100% in Hernand.
From here on, rest between jobs: every timer on this route counts in-game hours.

meanwhile.text: Gold Bars from the Wildlife Park pay for the Blessings.

phases.label: Build the dispatch engine
phases.why: Estate Security turns food into Camp Funds on Repeat. Supply dispatches keep the food coming, excavations pay the largest lumps, and Grey-0 workers fill the routine slots.

steps.text: Set one food mission for every food-hungry money mission, then add stone and timber.
Put every manor's security mission on Repeat.
Send specialists to excavations: 37,000 a Tinkerton run.
Build Grey-0 workers once food and funds balance after a full cycle.

meanwhile.text: Farm Golden Apples and ore while the timers run.

phases.label: Open the trade routes
phases.why: Patch 1.16 quadrupled Royal post prices and added 133 posts. One wagon of Salt sold for 84,450 Silver, and every Silver donated becomes 10 Camp Funds.

steps.text: Find the buyer on the Trade tab, then load; never drive back empty.
Feed each Royal court the good on its list.

meanwhile.text: Spare Silver between runs can sit at Beighen's Five-Card table.

phases.label: Convert at the best rate
phases.why: Ships, leases and Blessings cost Camp Funds. Silver converts at 10 to 1 since 2.01; a whole Gold Bar was measured at 50,000, ten times its Silver value. Test one bar, then convert the cheaper way.

steps.text: Donate one bar and read the counter. At 50,000, donate bars whole and keep Silver for Kliff.
Bars you will not donate go in at Medium risk; Bonds only past 100 spare bars.

phases.label: Finish Pailune
phases.why: The final camp doubles farm and ranch space, which is more food for the dispatch engine, and 1,000 storage slots hold cargo between runs.

steps.text: Finish the rebuild if it is still open.
Clear the quest checklist, save manually, and move with Serkis's The Return Home.

phases.label: Lease before you sail
phases.why: Facilities are the DLC's first income: the Timberham lease costs 15,000 and pays daily while you are at sea. Upkeep is daily too, so lease only what your roster can staff.

steps.text: Lease Timberham and reach Popularity Level 3 with low prices.
Lease the businesses your staff can run: Cooking, Smithing, Tailoring, Woodworking.

phases.label: Build the first ship, buy the second
phases.why: The quest-built Small Greymane Ship holds 14, the same as the 40,000 Small Hernandian. Skip that purchase; the Medium at 1.2M is the first ship that adds cargo space.

steps.text: Build it from a port's Missions menu: five comrades, 12 hours.
Crew First Mate, Rigger and Lookout; keep Deckhands for the islands.
Buy the Medium at 1.2M; the Large at 6M only when routes fill 22 slots.

phases.label: Pioneer the islands
phases.why: Each anchorage adds missions, shops and a ship teleport point. Castles come last: they cost funds and stock and pay nothing back.

steps.text: Pioneer Auronui from its Anchorage, then Samora and Winding Island.
Rebuild a castle only from surplus: 20 comrades away for 15 days.
